get.summary: Get or lazy-create the caller's user config
get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's `user_config` preferences (display name, marketing email opt-in, and Terms of Service agreement timestamp). If no row exists yet, inserts defaults (`display_name` empty string, `marketing_emails_opt_in` false, `marketing_emails_opt_in_at` null, `terms_of_service_agreed_at` null) and returns that row.
**Lazy-create pattern:** empty `user_config` rows are created on first GET (not via a Kratos registration webhook). This keeps Kratos auth-only and the product DB responsible for user-facing prefs.

200.description: Caller's user config. Always present after this call (created with defaults when missing).

user_config.description: Owner-only preferences for the signed-in user.

401.description: Unauthorized - missing or invalid auth headers, or not logged in.

user-config.description: Product-owned preferences for the signed-in user (owner-only). Keyed by Kratos identity id. Holds display name, marketing email consent, and Terms of Service agreement — not auth traits. Kratos owns identity/credentials/sessions; this resource is the Kratos-minimal product DB pattern.

user_id.description: Kratos identity id of the owning user.

display_name.description: How the user appears to themselves and to others. May be empty after lazy-create until the first save; PUT requires a non-empty trimmed value.

marketing_emails_opt_in.description: Explicit consent for product/marketing email. Defaults to false until the user opts in.

marketing_emails_opt_in_at.description: When the user most recently opted into marketing email. Null when never opted in or after opting out (cleared when `marketing_emails_opt_in` becomes false).

terms_of_service_agreed_at.description: When the user agreed to the Terms of Service. Null until agreement is recorded (typically via PUT with `terms_of_service_agreed_at: "now"`). Once set, later preference updates do not clear or overwrite it.

created_at.description: When the user config row was created.

updated_at.description: When the user config row was last updated.

code.description: A short, machine-readable error code, for when HTTP status codes are not sufficient.

message.description: A human-readable description of the error.
message.example: The requested resource could not be found.
